comment: Professor Marquardt is one of the nicest professors out there, but it is true his assignments can be a little vague. The tests take a lot of studying because of how much material there is, but all the information comes from his powerpoint. In comparison, there is relatively little to no homework outside of class. Definitely would not avoid him.

Very vague in his explanation of expectations for harshly graded projects, which account for the majority of your grade. Not helpful if most of the class needs to schedule office hours to explain expectations for a project. This could have been laid out better in a project handout. Not the best or clearest professor I've had in the business school.

I would say that he is one of the nicest professors I have had, and the assignments are really interesting (Jonas Brothers project, work with marketing at Nike), but sometimes is vague with assignments. All you have to do is go to his office and he will explain further. really great guy.

Took his Principles of Marketing class. The most inspirational professor that I've had thus far; if anyone cares about his students, it's him. He applies relevant concepts in class lectures as a means for you to keep up to date with contemporary business issues. Given me countless career advice. Tests are hard, but very helpful during office hrs.
Agree what has been said: A really nice professor, but I didn't learn anything from his class.. His assignments are super vague and would not really recommend..

He is the NICEST person on this planet, which makes it hard for me to say he's a terrible teacher. But he is. Extremely vague when assigning things, and expects so much from students. Didn't give an assignment sheet for the semester-long project and expected every group to know exactly what to do. Not helpful.

Such a subpar teacher. You really won't learn much for this class. Does not teach material well. The tests are pretty easy though but be prepared for a unnecessary group final project that is graded extremely harshly. Try taking this class with a different professor.
Tons of work and learn nothing

To start off, I will say it is a marketing class, so you don't really learn anything. His tests are purely memorization of a hundred slides pretty much so you pretty much memorize useless information and you will do fine. A few group projects with not a lot of guidelines, overall, would probably recommend for non-marketing majors

Marquardt means well, he really does. His slides are organized (exactly copied from the textbook) and he reads them off during class. He answers questions vaguely and class time is spent copying down the slides word-for-word. Tests are impossible (memorization)and group project assignments are extensive. It's a fine class, but you don't learn much.
